chunks: He shall be at the head of his people on the Day of Resurrection, and drive them into Hell like cattle driven to water -- what an evil watering-place to reach!
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when a leader drives his people to Hell on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to highlight the accountability of political and religious leaders who lead the masses astray, emphasizing that their guidance results in collective damnation. The metaphor of 'watering' (ward) underscores the inevitability and finality of their destination, serving as a warning for those in authority to ensure their leadership aligns with divine truth rather than personal desire.
